content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Atlanta

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and measurable project-management experience before you apply. Review PMI's specific requirements for your background—secondary degree holders and bachelor's degree holders face different thresholds. Granite PM Academy's advisors can clarify where you stand.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Boot Camp. Our Atlanta-focused cohorts meet synchronously over several weeks, letting you learn from experienced instructors without relocating. You'll receive the formal contact hours PMI requires to sit for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing boot camp, submit your formal PMP application directly to PMI and pay the associated examination fee. PMI will verify your education and experience. Granite PM Academy provides guidance on the application process to ensure accuracy and avoid delays.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and instructor office hours—to solidify your knowledge. When ready, schedule your computer-based PMP exam through PMI's testing partner. Our support doesn't end when boot camp does; we're here before you test.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, you'll hold the PMP credential for three years. During this cycle, earn professional development units (PDUs) through approved training, volunteering, or continuing education. Plan ahead to meet PMI's renewal requirements before your certification expires.
